world.foundationDescription: Define how the world operates, how it is photographed, and what must never appear. Once locked, these rules govern every character and shot downstream.
world.colorScript: Faction colors, ownership of light, and forbidden colors
world.materialRules: Primary materials, wear, and aging rules
world.architectureLanguage: Architecture, shape, symbols, and spatial language
world.cameraFormat: Aspect, lens, grain, black level, and color strategy
world.forbiddenElements: Explicitly excluded styles, symbols, and designs
world.referencesDescription: Upload color, material, architecture, and lighting references. They are design evidence only; people, text, and logos are not copied.
world.assetsDescription: The four plates separately answer world thesis, faction color, material aging, and architectural symbols. Every plate must complete and pass review.
world.rejectionPrompt: Describe the rejection, such as unclear faction hierarchy, implausible materials, or conflicting architecture.
world.canonGateDescription: Complete every rule, generate all four assets, and approve each plate before locking World Canon. Casting unlocks only after this gate passes.

casting.lifeHistory: Life history visible in the face
casting.generateHint: Every candidate records the actual model, provider, prompt, dimensions, and seed support. A seed is not identity; the selected face becomes the Canon reference.
casting.worldRequired: Complete and lock World Canon in Phase 00 first
casting.worldLocked: World Canon loaded. Casting prompts inherit its story and emotional rules.
casting.generateFailed: Unable to create the casting batch

face.canonRequired: Lock a Casting choice before starting Face Bible
face.identityAnchors: Identity anchors: face shape, eye spacing, nose, mouth, jaw, hairline and natural asymmetry
face.referenceOnly: The Canon image defines identity only
face.rejectionPrompt: Describe the rejection, such as nose drift, age change, or a different identity.
face.lockHint: All ten assets must complete and pass individual review before a formal FACE ID can be created. Rejected assets require a new batch.
face.modelHint: Only enabled models with declared reference-image support are listed. A seed is recorded but never treated as identity.
face.generateFailed: Failed to create Face Bible batch
face.lockFailed: Face Bible is not ready to lock

hair.prerequisite: Complete and lock Face Bible first
hair.prerequisiteHint: Hair Design may change hair only. The approved front-facing Face Bible asset is the sole identity authority.
hair.partingAndHairline: Parting, hairline, and face visibility rules
hair.storyRequirements: Character arc, class, and story-state requirements
hair.modelHint: Only enabled models that can consume identity and hair references together are listed. Exploration uses Face ID; validation assigns image 1 to identity and image 2 to hair.
hair.exploreDescription: Keep face, camera, white background, and studio treatment fixed. Change only silhouette, parting, length, texture, and construction—without costume or accessories.
hair.validationTitle: Hair validation · construction, motion, and story states
hair.validationDescription: Use Face ID plus the selected hair reference to validate front, profile, back, backlight, walking, wind, formal, and distressed states.
hair.rejectionPrompt: Describe the rejection, such as face drift, changed parting, contradictory back construction, or implausible motion.
hair.lockHint: All eight validation assets must complete and pass review before a formal HAIR ID is created for costume, props, and downstream shots.
hair.lockFailed: Hair assets are not ready to lock

board.title: Stage asset board
board.description: Once upstream canon is approved, this board will load the relevant prompts, references, and review state.

inspector.title: Development control
inspector.lockPolicyDescription: Only assets approved in the current phase can become the single source of truth for the next phase.
inspector.recordNotice: The connected version will record model version, seed, dimensions, prompt, and references.

research.title: Reference Research
research.objective: Build credible references for the character, period, materials, culture, and cinematic language before designing.
research.gate: References are traceable, coherent, and clearly support the character and world.

world.title: World Bible
world.objective: Define the color, material, architecture, faction, and technology rules shared by every character.
world.gate: The world rules can constrain downstream prompts and identify designs that do not belong in the film.

casting.title: Casting
casting.objective: Select the face that can carry the role without costume, accessories, abilities, or a dramatic setting.
deliverables: Seed and model record per candidate
casting.gate: One distinctive face remains stable across angles and can carry the character's emotional range.

face.title: Face Bible and Identity Lock
face.objective: Turn the selected face into an identity standard that survives changes in angle, expression, and lens.
deliverables: Skin, eye, nose, lip, and ear detail
face.gate: Every view reads as the same person without age, ethnicity, or facial proportion drift.

hair.title: Hair Design
hair.objective: Keep identity fixed while exploring hairstyles that support arc, class, and story state.
hair.gate: Core and story variants are clear without changing the locked facial identity.

costume.title: Costume Design
costume.objective: Create silhouette, function, and material history from the World Bible and character arc.
costume.gate: Silhouette, function, class, and material origin are explainable and obey world rules.

accessory.title: Accessories and Signature Props
accessory.objective: Build icons, accessories, weapons, and carry items that identify the character independently.
accessory.gate: Every prop has a story or functional reason beyond decoration.

silhouette.title: Silhouette Validation
silhouette.objective: Test whether the character remains uniquely identifiable without face or material detail.
silhouette.gate: Characters do not merge in a lineup and remain readable in wide shots and backlight.

expression.title: Cinematic Expression
expression.objective: Design playable emotions around story beats rather than generic happy, sad, angry, and afraid poses.
expression.gate: Emotion is credible while actor identity remains stable without beautification or facial drift.

ability.title: Ability and VFX Language
ability.objective: Break powers into filmable, generatable visual rules and progressive states.
ability.gate: The ability fits character, world rules, and cinematography and can be divided into shots.

hero.title: Hero Shot
hero.objective: Combine the locked face, hair, costume, props, and ability into a definitive cinematic image.
hero.gate: All locked assets are integrated correctly and the frame communicates role and tone.

turnaround.title: Character Turnaround
turnaround.objective: Create the shared character standard used by modeling, generation, and the production team.
turnaround.gate: The sheet has no view contradictions and is sufficient as the official downstream reference.

evolution.title: Costume Evolution
evolution.objective: Map costume, hair, injuries, and prop continuity across the story timeline.
evolution.gate: Every change maps to a story event with explicit continuity rules between shots.

integration.title: Scene Integration and Lighting
integration.objective: Place the approved character in key scenes to test scale, color temperature, materials, and faction readability.
integration.gate: The character belongs in the scene and keeps stable materials, skin tone, and identity.

video.title: Video Bible
video.objective: Define motion, performance, camera, and consistency references before entering video models.
video.gate: Face, costume, body, performance, and physics remain coherent across continuous shots.
